text: {"version":1,"kind":"conversation","reading":"The user asks for a subjective recommendation (which of the ten ranked players to build a team around, and why), which is a judgment call rather than a governed measurement.","measures":[],"groupBy":[],"display":[],"filters":[],"expectedShape":"lookup","unresolved":[],"provenance":{},"reply":"\"Who to build a team around\" is a judgment call that this project can't settle on its own — it holds box-score lines for calendar 2016–2017 (points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, shooting, turnovers, results), not contracts, age, injuries, salary, or fit. What the previous result does show: James Harden led the 2017 top ten in points per game (30.08) with strong assists (9.79); Russell Westbrook averaged a triple-double (29.03 / 10.14 / 10.02); LeBron James combined 28.20 points with the most games played (100), i.e., the most durable. If you want the data to narrow the choice, I can extend the same ranking with shooting efficiency (field goals made ÷ attempted, three-point rate), turnovers per game, steals and blocks per game, or the team's win rate in games each player played — just say which criteria matter to you."}
